messages:
alert-bot: :rotating_light: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed across us-east-1 serving fleet. P95 spiking from 120ms -> 2.1s, P99 ~8s. Error rate ~3.4% (baseline 0.04%). Paging matt (oncall) and ashley (sre).

matt (oncall): on it. grabbing context. any deploys in last 30m?

deploy-bot: deploy completed: release/2026-03-15-12:04 (miguel) — finished 1769999802. Canary 5% -> 100% at 12:07.

miguel (runtime): that was the kernel selector change + kv-cache tweak. rolling canary finished ~12:07. rolling back if needed.

ashley (sre): confirming: traffic graph shows spike aligning with canary->prod cutover. p95 jump immediate. lots of gateway timeouts (502/504) hitting proxy layer and then runtime.

matt (oncall): tag customer-impact. jess, any support tickets/alerts from customers?

jess (support): seeing ~12 support pings mentioning slow responses across apps; 2 customers reported timeouts and retries. internal telemetry shows retry storms from some older SDK versions.

ashley (sre): quick triage checklist: 1) revert deploy 2) enable fallback routing to stable model variant 3) scale front-end proxy pool 4) rate-limit noisy SDKs. Which is fastest?

miguel (runtime): fastest is revert. rollback command below: 
```
./deploy revert --release 2026-03-15-12:04 --force
```
I can run that now.

matt (oncall): do it. also enable circuit breaker on gateway for 8s threshold to prevent cascading. samir can you patch LB?

samir (platform): applying circuit-breaker rule now. patch in progress — will post once active.

ops-bot: Applying gateway circuit-breaker: threshold=8s, consecutive_errors=5.

matt (oncall): miguel, execute rollback and share status. ashley, monitor p95/p99 and error%. jess, notify the two affected customers we're investigating with ETA ~15m. irene, heads-up for product/customer comms.

miguel (runtime): running rollback now. output: 
```
Rolling back to release/2026-03-14-21:10...\nStopping rollout traffic to release/2026-03-15-12:04...\nVerifying instance drain... ok\nActivating release/2026-03-14-21:10... ok\nRollback complete: 1769999987
```

ashley (sre): p95 -> 140ms within 90s of rollback. error rate dropping: 3.4% -> 0.12% -> 0.05% (now). p99 back to ~300ms. gateway timeouts largely resolved but still a few residual 502s.

samir (platform): circuit-breaker active. added temporary LB pool autoscale +15% to absorb retry bursts.

matt (oncall): rerun the synthetic smoke across top routes and report. ashley?

ashley (sre): smoke results: text-gen route ok, chat streaming ok, embedding endpoints within normal latency. no increased queue depth.

jess (support): told customers rollback complete and mitigation in progress. will open postmortem ticket and collect affected request IDs from their reports. reaction :white_check_mark:

irene (product): thanks. capturing for customer comms: timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation. need an ETA for root cause RCA.

miguel (runtime): initial hypothesis: kernel selector change combined with new kv-cache expiry policy caused pathological cache misses under production request distribution; that exposed a slow path in a new fallback kernel that caused long tail latency and timeouts at the proxy. I need logs + flamegraphs to confirm.

ashley (sre): attaching quick logs (excerpt): 
```
[12:08:19] runtime: serve_request id=abc123 latency=8200ms path=/v1/generate kernel=fallback-kernel
[12:08:20] proxy: upstream_connect_timeout id=abc123 backend=runtime-42
[12:08:21] runtime: serve_request id=def456 latency=7100ms kernel=fallback-kernel
```

matt (oncall): good. next steps: 1) preserve all runtime nodes (do not autoscale down) 2) capture heap/cpu profiles from nodes that served long requests 3) revert kernel selector change in branch and run offline tests with production traces 4) schedule hotfix if confirmed.

miguel (runtime): will collect traces and profile dump. posting commands: 
```
for NODE in $(cat affected_nodes.txt); do ssh $NODE "sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30" && scp $NODE:/tmp/perf.data ./perf-$NODE.data; done
```

ops-bot: Preserving nodes: autoscaler suspended for affected pool for 2h.

ashley (sre): monitoring shows one remaining hotspot node with elevated GC pauses. collecting GC logs now.

matt (oncall): if RCA confirms kernel fallback slow path, let's plan a staged re-release with the kernel selector disabled and an A/B where 10% traffic uses original path for 1h. No full rollouts until validated.

irene (product): product asks for a brief incident summary for customers: what happened, who was affected, what we did, next steps. Can you draft initial note? Keep it short.

jess (support): drafting now. noting impacted timeframe: 12:04–12:09 production spike; customer retries increased between 12:06–12:12; full mitigation by 12:10 after rollback.

matt (oncall): good. handoff to ashley and miguel for RCA. I'll remain available for questions. open incident postmortem and assign to miguel (owner) + ashley (SRE reviewer). tag severity: Sev2.

miguel (runtime): created postmortem ticket INC-2026-0315-01 with timeline, artifacts, sample traces. planning local reproduce with production trace replay tomorrow.

ashley (sre): final check: all alert thresholds back to normal. enabling autoscaler after confirming no further traffic anomalies. ops-bot do that in 15m.

ops-bot: Autoscaler resume scheduled at 15m.

matt (oncall): thanks team. follow up: include unit/regression test for kernel fallback performance in CI and add a canary-level perf check when kernel selector config changes. Closing live thread, moving to postmortem channel. :lock:
